# Solid Symposium 2027 (SoSy 27)

> The 5th Solid Symposium: the annual meeting of the Solid community, held at
> SQUARE on the University of St.Gallen campus in Switzerland on 10–12 May 2027.

- **Official site:** https://sosy2027.org/ (single page; canonical URL, no other pages)
- **Dates:** Solid Open Day on digital sovereignty Mon 10 May 2027; symposium Tue 11 – Wed 12 May 2027
- **Venue:** SQUARE, University of St.Gallen, Guisanstrasse 20, 9010 St.Gallen, Switzerland
- **Language:** English (the public evening event on 10 May is in German)
- **Contact:** fuso@unisg.ch
- **Organiser:** Solid Symposium 2027 Organisation Committee
- **Organised by:** Future Society Hub (FuSo, https://futuresociety.ch/), the
  Institute of Computer Science (ICS-HSG, https://ics.unisg.ch/) and the
  Institute for Law and Economics (ILE-HSG, https://ile.unisg.ch/en/), all at
  the University of St.Gallen

## About Solid

Solid is a specification developed in the W3C Solid Community Group and
initiated by Sir Tim Berners-Lee. It keeps a person's data in a personal online
datastore — a Pod — that they control, and lets applications read and write that
data with their permission instead of each application holding its own copy.
See https://solidproject.org/.

## Solid and digital sovereignty

Digital sovereignty is the ability of people, organisations and public
institutions to decide for themselves over their data and the digital
infrastructure they depend on. Solid supports it by separating data from
applications: data lives in a Pod its owner chooses — self-hosted, at their
institution or with a provider they trust — and the owner grants and revokes
each application's access through open W3C standards. Changing an application
or a Pod provider therefore does not mean losing the data or being locked in.
Digital sovereignty is the theme of the public Solid Open Day on 10 May 2027.

## Programme shape

- **Mon 10 May 2027 — Solid Open Day: Digital Sovereignty (open to the public):** a
  public day on who controls our data and how Solid puts that control back with
  people, organisations and public institutions. Student hackathon on building
  for digital sovereignty with Solid; public evening event on digital
  sovereignty, in German; onboarding session for creating your first Solid Pod.
- **Tue 11 May 2027 — Day One:** keynote; peer-reviewed papers in two parallel
  tracks; poster and demo lightning talks; community sessions; hackathon
  pitches and award; evening event.
- **Wed 12 May 2027 — Day Two:** keynote; peer-reviewed papers in two parallel
  tracks; community sessions; closing, awards and handover to the next
  edition.

## Call for Sessions (open)

The Solid community is invited to propose sessions for 11 or 12 May 2027:
https://sosy2027.org/#call-for-sessions

- **Format:** one or two 75-minute slots (more on request), in any form —
  soliciting papers, talks, panel discussions, demos, tutorials, hands-on
  workshops, hackathons. Session organisers choose the theme, confirm speakers
  and gather contributions; the symposium organisers provide the room, coffee
  breaks, lunch, a social event and a programme of keynotes.
- **Proposal:** max. three pages, any reasonable format, by email to
  fuso@unisg.ch. Include title and abstract; (co-)organisers and affiliations;
  prospective PC members if any; description with preliminary agenda and
  potential speakers, and a preference for 11 or 12 May; relation to Solid,
  intended audience, suitability for newcomers and expected attendance; any
  non-standard equipment needs.
- **Deadline:** 25 November 2026 (AoE). Notifications on a rolling basis, by
  2 December 2026 at the latest.
- **Accepted sessions** set up their own landing page, linked from sosy2027.org.
- **Topic suggestions:** Solid architecture; Solid and its users; agents on and
  about Solid; legal aspects (data protection, governance); authoring tools;
  open-source Solid projects; applications (industry, research, public
  entities); business cases; medical personal data; self-publishing; data
  spaces; digital wallets; security and privacy; evolving Web standards behind
  Solid; any other Solid topic.

## Key dates

- **Open now** — Call for Sessions
- **25 Nov 2026** — session proposal deadline (AoE)
- **2 Dec 2026** — session notifications, at the latest
- **Autumn 2026** — call for contributions opens (papers, posters, demos)
- **Feb 2027** — submission deadline
- **Mar 2027** — notifications to authors
- **Mar 2027** — registration opens
- **10–12 May 2027** — Solid Symposium 2027

The Call for Sessions dates are fixed; the remaining dates are indicative and
are fixed as each call is published.
